task.description: Hard gate on lib/letflow/design/iss0400-nested-parallel-gateway-fix.md, CODE-DESIGNER's fix design for ISS-0400. This design's own risk class is explicitly the same one that produced TWO real BLOCKER-severity catches on the immediately-preceding, closely-related ISS-0398 design (a naive-visited-set DoS-shaped exponential blowup, and a memo-key-unsoundness defect under legal cycles) -- read lib/letflow/design/iss0398-walk-to-gateway-fix.md's own account of both catches before gating this one, and adversarially re-derive whether this design's memo-sharing/pass-through claim (no new memo entry written under the nested split's own node_id) actually holds, rather than accepting the design doc's own worked trace as sufficient. Specifically interrogate: (1) does resolve_nested_split/3, as specified, genuinely never introduce a fresh memo key that could suffer the same unsoundness ISS-0398's own memo-key catch found, under some cyclic or deeply-nested graph shape the design's own worked example doesn't cover; (2) is the termination argument for arbitrary nesting depth actually sound, not just plausible, given graph.ex's @max_nodes 500 bound cited as the ceiling; (3) does the design's claim that all existing ISS-0398 fixtures are unaffected (zero :split-role PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes) actually check out against the real fixture files, not just asserted; (4) is the :dead_end failure-propagation choice for inner-split-resolution-failure actually correct across every call site that pattern-matches on collect_leaf_gateways/3's return shape, not just the ones the design doc discusses. Standard WF-02 Step 1b design-gate checks also apply in full (every acceptance criterion mapped to a concrete design element, no TBD/deferral language, no .ex function bodies present, all cross-module deps named).
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion on step-02-code-designer.json's task block is independently verified against a concrete design element, not accepted from CODE-DESIGNER's own summary

The memo-key-soundness claim is adversarially re-derived against at least one graph shape not already covered by the design doc's own worked trace, specifically hunting for a recurrence of ISS-0398's own memo-key-unsoundness defect class
The nesting-depth termination argument is checked against graph.ex's actual @max_nodes bound, not merely cited
The 'zero :split-role PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes in existing fixtures' non-regression claim is verified by actually reading the fixture files, not accepted as stated
Every call site of collect_leaf_gateways/3 (or of find_matching_join/2, whichever changes) is checked against the :dead_end propagation choice for correctness
No .ex implementation bodies present in the design doc
Verdict is PASS or FAIL with every issue at BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR severity named specifically, not a general impression

result.summary:
FAIL -- BLOCKER: resolve_nested_split/3 as specified (design §2.3) will infinite-recurse (never terminate, contradicting the design's own §3.4 'Totality (never raises)' claim) on a legal, CHK-01..CHK-19-valid graph the design's own fixture 3 was intended to cover but does not actually exercise correctly, because the algorithm as literally specified does not behave the way §3.3 claims it does.

Adversarial re-derivation (acceptance criterion 2 of this handoff): constructed a graph -- outer_split (PARALLEL_GATEWAY, out_degree 2): branch 0 direct to outer_join (control); branch 1: outer_split -> A -> inner_split (PARALLEL_GATEWAY, out_degree 2, :split role) -> edge a: inner_split -> ia -> A (back-edge to A, an ANCESTOR ON THE OUTER WALK'S OWN CALL CHAIN, still logically in-progress -- A's own call frame has not returned, it is blocked waiting on inner_split's resolution); edge b: inner_split -> ib -> inner_join (PARALLEL_GATEWAY, join-role) -> post -> outer_join. Traced the design's own specified algorithm step by step:

1. Outer walk reaches A (plain node, step 5): index[A]=0, pushed, stack=[A], stack_set={A}.
2. A's edge -> inner_split. collect_leaf_gateways(inner_split, state) -> step 4 -> gateway_role == :split (out_degree 2) -> design's step-4 :split arm fires resolve_nested_split(g, inner_split, state), called WHILE A IS STILL ON stack/stack_set (A's own call frame is the immediate, still-open caller).
3. Design §2.3 (line 155, verbatim): resolve_nested_split/3 'resets only index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index between the nested split's own sibling branches' BEFORE folding over inner_split's own branches -- this wipes A out of stack_set.
4. Inner fold, edge a: ia fresh (inner-fold index 0, pushed) -> edge to A. collect_leaf_gateways(A, state): is A in memo? No. Is A in stack_set? NO -- wiped by the reset in step 3. The step-2 on-stack/live-back-edge check therefore FAILS TO FIRE for a genuine, still-live back-edge to an ancestor whose call frame is still on the actual Elixir call stack.
5. Falls through to step 5: A is treated as FRESH -- assigned a new index in the inner fold's own numbering, re-pushed, and A's own outgoing edge (A -> inner_split) is followed AGAIN, recursing back into inner_split.
6. inner_split is not memoized (design's own §3.1 requires resolve_nested_split/3 to never write memo[gw_node.id] for the split itself) and is not on the (wiped) stack_set either -- so collect_leaf_gateways(inner_split, ...) re-dispatches through step 4 -> :split -> resolve_nested_split/3 is invoked AGAIN, recursively, on the SAME inner_split node, with ANOTHER reset of stack bookkeeping.
7. This repeats without bound: A <-> inner_split forms an infinite regress under the specified algorithm. No node count or @max_nodes bound stops it, because the mechanism that is supposed to detect and close this cycle (stack_set on-stack membership) is destroyed by the reset exactly at the boundary where it is needed.

This directly falsifies design §3.4's 'Totality (never raises)' claim (which asserts no new possibility of a raise/non-termination is introduced) and exposes a real, load-bearing INTERNAL CONTRADICTION in the design document itself: §2.3 (line 155) specifies resolve_nested_split/3 RESETS index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index before its own fold (identical wording to find_matching_join/2's top-level-only-safe reset discipline), while §3.3 later asserts 'state.stack/stack_set are shared across this recursive boundary exactly like memo is' (used to justify why an {:open, lowlink} result can legitimately propagate out of resolve_nested_split/3 in fixture 3's scenario). These two statements cannot both be true of the same specified algorithm -- and the trace above shows the reset (§2.3's literal instruction) is what actually governs, producing non-termination, not the sharing §3.3 claims.

The design's own fixture 3 (nested_split_reentrant_cycle_graph/0, §4) was explicitly intended to exercise exactly this shape ('a live back-edge that reaches back out of the nested split's own resolution into an ancestor still on the outer walk's shared stack') and its assertion note even flags 'TEST-DESIGNER should also verify... that this does not raise or infinite-loop' -- but per the trace above, the algorithm AS SPECIFIED would actually infinite-loop on this fixture (or a graph shape one edge simpler than it, as constructed above), not merely risk it. The find_matching_join/2 precedent this design reuses verbatim is safe to reset between BRANCHES of one TOP-LEVEL call specifically because ISS-0398 design §2.2.3 proves a top-level call's own stack is always fully unwound before it returns (nothing is left open for a sibling branch to inherit) -- but resolve_nested_split/3 is invoked MID-FLIGHT, from inside an already-open outer-walk call frame (the nested split's own immediate predecessor node, e.g. A, has NOT returned), so the top-level-only safety argument the reset discipline depends on does not transfer to this new recursive boundary. This is the same defect FAMILY as ISS-0398's own memo-key-unsoundness catch (shared mutable traversal state incorrectly reset/isolated at a boundary where liveness must be preserved), recurring at the new nested-recursion boundary this design introduces, not an identical instance of it -- exactly the risk class this handoff's task.description named as the primary thing to hunt for.

Other acceptance criteria independently verified and found sound (recorded so rework does not need to redo this work): (2) the @max_nodes 500 bound and the >=3-nodes-per-nesting-level arithmetic (design §3.4) is correct against graph.ex:158 (@max_nodes 500 confirmed by direct read) -- this part of the termination argument is fine in isolation, it is the RECURSION-WITHOUT-PROGRESS defect above that defeats it, since the defect causes unbounded RE-exploration of the same 2 nodes rather than bounded exploration of new ones, so no node-count bound can catch it. (3) The 'zero :split-role PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes in existing fixtures' claim was verified directly against test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs's actual fixture bodies (all 6: three_branch_graph/0, branch_with_exclusive_gateway_graph/0, ambiguous_branch_dead_ends_graph/0, diamond_chain_graph/1, cyclic_escape_graph/0 + reversed twin, pure_cycle_no_escape_graph/0, read in full) -- confirmed true, every PARALLEL_GATEWAY node in every fixture is either the never-revisited outer split entry point or a real join (in_degree>1, out_degree<=1); this claim holds. (4) collect_leaf_gateways/3's own call sites (find_matching_join/2's fold at transition.ex:820-837, fold_outgoing_edges/4's recursive call at transition.ex:987-1004) both already destructure the generic {tag, leaves, state} triple and treat any non-singleton-or-non-{:gateway,_} leaves value uniformly as a failure -- the :dead_end-folding choice for inner-resolution-failure (design §3.3) is consistent with every real call site; no call site would need a distinct tag. No .ex implementation bodies present in the design doc (confirmed by direct read of the full document -- only @spec fences and prose, matching ISS-0398's own convention).

Routes back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework. The fix needs a genuinely different mechanism for detecting a live back-edge from inside a nested split's own fold back to an outer-walk ancestor -- e.g. NOT resetting stack/stack_set/index/lowlink at the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary at all (only resetting them between find_matching_join/2's own TOP-LEVEL branches, where §2.2.3's unwound-stack proof actually applies), and instead giving each nested fold its own freshly-numbered index space that composes with (rather than replaces) the outer walk's live stack_set membership check -- or some other mechanism that CODE-DESIGNER must design and re-prove sound against this exact counterexample, not merely re-assert.

issues.description: resolve_nested_split/3 (design §2.3, lib/letflow/design/iss0400-nested-parallel-gateway-fix.md) resets index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index before folding over a nested split's own sibling branches, but is invoked mid-flight from inside an already-open outer-walk call frame (the nested split's own immediate predecessor is still on-stack, its call frame not yet returned) rather than between top-level find_matching_join/2 branches (where the reset is proven safe by ISS-0398 design section 2.2.3's unwound-stack argument). This destroys live back-edge detection for outer-walk ancestors still genuinely in progress, causing the traversal to re-treat an already-in-progress ancestor as fresh and infinite-recurse when the nested split's own subgraph loops back to that ancestor (concrete counterexample and full trace in result.summary). This also contradicts design section 3.3's own claim that state.stack/stack_set are 'shared across this recursive boundary exactly like memo is' -- section 2.3 specifies a reset, not sharing; the two sections describe incompatible algorithms. Design's own fixture 3 (nested_split_reentrant_cycle_graph/0) was intended to catch exactly this and does not, because the algorithm as specified does not behave the way the design believes it does under that fixture.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for rework (WF-03 Step 2 retry) -- fix the stack/stack_set reset-vs-share contradiction between design sections 2.3 and 3.3 and re-prove termination against the A/inner_split back-edge counterexample in this handoff's result.summary before resubmitting.
